en: On the snowy day they played on the mountain for four hours and only came back in the evening.

q: 昨天雨下___三个小时。
zh: 昨天雨下了三个小时。
py: zuó tiān yǔ xià le sān gè xiǎo shí
en: It rained for three hours yesterday.
why: A stretch of rain that is over takes 了 between 下 and the duration. 过 would mean 'has ever rained for three hours', and 着 describes a continuing state, neither fits 昨天.

s: 去年冬天我去过哈尔滨两次。
s_py: qù nián dōng tiān wǒ qù guo hā ěr bīn liǎng cì
zh: 去年冬天我去过哈尔滨两次。
py: qù nián dōng tiān wǒ qù guo hā ěr bīn liǎng cì
en: I went to Harbin twice last winter.
why: A place name may come before the count, 去过哈尔滨两次, as well as after it. Both are fine.

q: 我感冒了，一个星期没出门___。
zh: 我感冒了，一个星期没出门了。
py: wǒ gǎn mào le yī gè xīng qī méi chū mén le
en: I caught a cold and haven't gone out for a week.
why: 一个星期 before 没 plus final 了 says 'for a week up to now'. 过 would change it to 'never went out', 的 and 着 do not close the clause.

q: 李老师教了我们___。
zh: 李老师教了我们两年。
py: lǐ lǎo shī jiāo le wǒ men liǎng nián
en: Mr. Li taught us for two years.
why: After the pronoun object comes the duration 两年. 两月 is not a length (it needs 个), 两点 is two o'clock, and 两次 counts occasions rather than the time taught.

zh: 大雨下了整整三天。
py: dà yǔ xià le zhěng zhěng sān tiān
en: The heavy rain lasted a full three days.
why: The duration 整整三天 follows 下了. It cannot go in front of the verb as a time-when.

q: 我们明天___去公园。
zh: 我们明天两点去公园。
py: wǒ men míng tiān liǎng diǎn qù gōng yuán
en: We are going to the park at two o'clock tomorrow.
why: 去公园 needs a point in time before the verb: 两点 is two o'clock. 两个小时, 两年 and 两天 are lengths and cannot stand in the time-when slot.

src_py: wǒ men sān diǎn liáo tiān
task: Say we chatted for three hours.
zh: 我们聊了三个小时的天。
py: wǒ men liáo le sān gè xiǎo shí de tiān
en: We chatted for three hours.
why: The length goes after 聊了, with 的 linking it to the object 天. The time-when 三点 became a length 三个小时 and moved after the verb.

s: 我们昨天聊天了两个小时。
s_py: wǒ men zuó tiān liáo tiān le liǎng gè xiǎo shí
zh: 我们昨天聊了两个小时的天。
py: wǒ men zuó tiān liáo le liǎng gè xiǎo shí de tiān
en: We chatted for two hours yesterday.
why: 聊天 splits when a duration is added: 聊了两个小时的天, or 聊天聊了两个小时. 了 cannot come after the whole word 聊天.

s_py: wǒ men sān gè xiǎo shí pá le shān
zh: 我们爬了三个小时的山。
py: wǒ men pá le sān gè xiǎo shí de shān
en: We climbed for three hours.
why: A length of time cannot stand before the verb as 'when'. It goes after 爬了.

q: 小李帮了___一个下午的忙。
zh: 小李帮了我一个下午的忙。
py: xiǎo lǐ bāng le wǒ yī gè xià wǔ de máng
en: Xiao Li helped me out for a whole afternoon.
why: The person goes right after 帮了, before the duration: 帮了我一个下午的忙. A possessive such as 我的 would turn the person into a modifier and break the sentence.

s_py: tā yóu yǒng yóu le bàn gè xiǎo shí
zh: 她游泳游了半个小时。
py: tā yóu yǒng yóu le bàn gè xiǎo shí
en: She swam for half an hour.
why: Repeating the verb is correct: 游泳游了半个小时. 了 sits on the second 游.

q: 明年夏天我想在海边住___一个月。
zh: 明年夏天我想在海边住一个月。
py: míng nián xià tiān wǒ xiǎng zài hǎi biān zhù yī gè yuè
en: Next summer I want to stay at the seaside for a month.
why: A plan is not finished, so no 了 follows 住; the duration still comes after the verb. 了, 着 and 过 all mark an action that has already happened or is under way.

q: 天气预报说明天有雨，你问___一下，要不要带伞？
zh: 天气预报说明天有雨，你问他一下，要不要带伞？
py: tiān qì yù bào shuō míng tiān yǒu yǔ nǐ wèn tā yī xià yào bu yào dài sǎn
en: The forecast says rain tomorrow, ask him whether he is bringing an umbrella.
why: A pronoun object goes before 一下, giving 问他一下. 他的 and 的他 are not possible there, and 了 would turn it into a completed action.

zh: 我三天没出门了。
py: wǒ sān tiān méi chū mén le
en: I haven't gone out for three days.
why: The length of not doing goes before 没, and the final 了 marks that it is still true. 没出门三天 is not the pattern.

zh: 雪已经下了三天了。
py: xuě yǐ jīng xià le sān tiān le
en: It has already been snowing for three days.
why: 已经 and the final 了 both say 'so far'. The duration follows 下了 and the second 了 ends the sentence.

zh: 他给我打了三次电话。
py: tā gěi wǒ dǎ le sān cì diàn huà
en: He phoned me three times.
why: The count 三次 goes between 打了 and the thing 电话. Putting 电话 before the count, as in English, is wrong.

s_py: wǒ men jiàn miàn guo liǎng cì
zh: 我们见过两次面。
py: wǒ men jiàn guo liǎng cì miàn
en: We have met twice.
why: 见面 is verb + object, so 过 and the count go between the two syllables. 见面过 cannot be stuck together.

s_py: tā gěi wǒ dǎ diàn huà le sān cì
zh: 他给我打了三次电话。
py: tā gěi wǒ dǎ le sān cì diàn huà
en: He phoned me three times.
why: 了 and the count belong right after 打, and the thing 电话 follows the count. 打电话了三次 splits the verb wrongly.

zh: 我只见过他两次。
py: wǒ zhǐ jiàn guo tā liǎng cì
en: I have only met him twice.
why: The pronoun 他 comes before the count 两次. 只 sits before the verb.

q: 他___去上海，要住两个星期。
zh: 他下个月去上海，要住两个星期。
py: tā xià gè yuè qù shàng hǎi yào zhù liǎng gè xīng qī
en: He is going to Shanghai next month and will stay for two weeks.
why: 去上海 needs a point in time before the verb: 下个月 is next month. 一个月, 三个月 and 半个月 are lengths and belong after a verb such as 住.

zh: 我们在雪地里玩了一个下午。
py: wǒ men zài xuě dì lǐ wán le yī gè xià wǔ
en: We played in the snow all afternoon.
why: The duration 一个下午 follows 玩了. The place phrase may come before or after the subject, but the length can never move in front of the verb.

task: Soften it: wait for a moment.
zh: 请你等一下。
py: qǐng nǐ děng yī xià
en: Please wait a moment.
why: 一下 after the verb makes the request short and polite: 等一下.

zh: 我去过两次北京。
py: wǒ qù guo liǎng cì běi jīng
en: I have been to Beijing twice.
why: A place name can sit either side of the count: 去过两次北京 or 去过北京两次. The count must follow 过 and cannot go before 去.

zh: 春天我们去过两次杭州。
py: chūn tiān wǒ men qù guo liǎng cì háng zhōu
en: We have been to Hangzhou twice in spring.
why: A place may follow the count or come before it, so both orders are fine, but the count must come after 过, not before 去.

q: 我们在咖啡馆坐了一个下午___，雨还没停。
zh: 我们在咖啡馆坐了一个下午了，雨还没停。
py: wǒ men zài kā fēi guǎn zuò le yī gè xià wǔ le yǔ hái méi tíng
en: We have been sitting in the cafe for a whole afternoon, and the rain still hasn't stopped.
why: 雨还没停 shows the sitting is still going on, so the duration is counted up to now with a final 了. 过, 着 and 的 cannot end the clause.

q: 因为天气太热，我们已经___没聚会了。
zh: 因为天气太热，我们已经半个月没聚会了。
py: yīn wèi tiān qì tài rè wǒ men yǐ jīng bàn gè yuè méi jù huì le
en: Because of the heat, we haven't had a get-together for half a month now.
why: The length 半个月 stands before 没 to say how long it has been. 半个月前 means 'half a month ago', a point in time, and 半个月的 would need a noun after it.

s: 我跟她见过两次面，还不熟。
s_py: wǒ gēn tā jiàn guo liǎng cì miàn hái bù shú
zh: 我跟她见过两次面，还不熟。
py: wǒ gēn tā jiàn guo liǎng cì miàn hái bù shú
en: I have met her twice and we aren't close yet.
why: 见面 splits around the count: 见过两次面. Correct.

s: 雪已经下了三天了，还没有停。
s_py: xuě yǐ jīng xià le sān tiān le hái méi yǒu tíng
zh: 雪已经下了三天了，还没有停。
py: xuě yǐ jīng xià le sān tiān le hái méi yǒu tíng
en: It has been snowing for three days now and it hasn't stopped.
why: The final 了 is correct because the three days are counted up to now and the snow continues.

zh: 朋友们很久没聚会了。
py: péng you men hěn jiǔ méi jù huì le
en: My friends haven't had a get-together for a long time.
why: 很久 is the length and must precede 没. It can come before or after the subject, but not after 聚会.

q: 我星期六上午___去爬山，大概爬三个小时。
zh: 我星期六上午九点去爬山，大概爬三个小时。
py: wǒ xīng qī liù shàng wǔ jiǔ diǎn qù pá shān dà gài pá sān gè xiǎo shí
en: On Saturday morning I'm going hiking at nine, for about three hours.
why: 去爬山 needs a point in time before it: 九点. The length 三个小时 follows the second 爬. 九个小时, 九年 and 九次 are lengths or counts that cannot name a clock time.

s: 我没在北京住三年，只住了两年。
s_py: wǒ méi zài běi jīng zhù sān nián zhǐ zhù le liǎng nián
zh: 我没在北京住三年，只住了两年。
py: wǒ méi zài běi jīng zhù sān nián zhǐ zhù le liǎng nián
en: I didn't live in Beijing for three years, only two.
why: Here 没 denies the amount: it is 'not three years', so the duration stays after the verb. This differs from 'for three years not'.

q: 上个月我请了两次___，都是因为感冒。
zh: 上个月我请了两次假，都是因为感冒。
py: shàng gè yuè wǒ qǐng le liǎng cì jià dōu shì yīn wèi gǎn mào
en: Last month I took leave twice, both times because of a cold.
why: 请假 is a split verb-object word, so the count goes between: 请了两次假. 请 does not pair with 病, 班 or 课 in this meaning.

zh: 今天下了一整天雨。
py: jīn tiān xià le yī zhěng tiān yǔ
en: It rained all day today.
why: With 雨 after the verb, the duration sits between 下了 and the object: 下了一整天雨. Or 雨 is fronted as topic: 今天雨下了一整天. 一整天 cannot go before the verb.

q: 夏天我去过两___北京，冬天还没去过。
zh: 夏天我去过两次北京，冬天还没去过。
py: xià tiān wǒ qù guo liǎng cì běi jīng dōng tiān hái méi qù guo
en: I have been to Beijing twice in summer, but not yet in winter.
why: Occasions are counted with 次 right after 过. 个 and 条 are measures for things, and 点 is for clock times, so they cannot count visits.

q: 我们___没见面了。
zh: 我们三个月没见面了。
py: wǒ men sān gè yuè méi jiàn miàn le
en: We haven't seen each other for three months.
why: 'Have not done it for three months' puts the length before 没: 三个月没见面了. 三月 is March, 三点 is three o'clock and 三次 counts occasions, so none gives 'three months'.

zh: 我来北京两年了。
py: wǒ lái běi jīng liǎng nián le
en: It has been two years since I came to Beijing.
why: 来 happens in an instant, so the time counts from it: Verb + Object + duration + 了.
